question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in execute-on-parse tool scheduling mode, and should it require tool concurrency-safety metadata before any early execution is allowed?
rationale: The source-level latency gap is clear, but changing when tools start is a core runtime and safety-policy decision rather than a narrow bug repair.

options.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
options.body: Keep this issue open for an owner design covering safety metadata, transcript ordering, approvals, hooks, cancellation, provider stream events, and regression proof.

options.title: Block On Safety Metadata
options.body: Treat implementation as dependent on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62962 or an equivalent concurrency-safety contract.

options.title: Defer Runtime Change
options.body: Keep current post-stream parallel batching as the only supported behavior if early execution is too risky for now.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for an owner design covering safety metadata, transcript ordering, approvals, hooks, cancellation, provider stream events, and regression proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties this person to the central agent-core loop and adjacent stream/tool execution surfaces.
